data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Adversarial examples in classification can be detected by discriminative tests that do not measure semantic verification, so discrimination is necessary but may not be sufficient.","A true/false pair tests one axis of error; systematic shared blind spots may lie on a different axis."],"overturn_conditions":["If a checker passes the adversarial pair test yet fails on a different false claim in the same error class, the test has false negatives and is insufficient.","If a restater can be trained to reject obvious false variants while still restating subtle ones, discriminative power is gameable."],"shared_structure":["Verification is operationally defined as discrimination between a claim and its negation.","Restatement is insensitive to the truth value of the claim.","Discriminative power is measurable within a single evaluation episode."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_002","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["For counting claims, construct count and count\u00b11; execute both; the checker must accept the correct count only.","For execution claims, run the program and a buggy variant; the checker must accept only the correct output.","The adversarial pair test transfers from classification to verification: the false positive rate on false claims measures independence."]},"claim":"The problem's framing creates a false dichotomy between author and checker. Genuine independent verification is best secured by adversarial perturbation of the claim itself: mutate the claim into a false variant, ask the checker to verify both, and demand that the checker accepts the true claim while rejecting the false one. This operationalizes independence as discriminative power rather than as engine separation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checker's discrimination is achieved by surface-level template matching (e.g., rejecting claims with specific tokens), it is not genuine verification of content.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If no natural false variant can be constructed for a claim, the discriminative test is inapplicable and engine separation remains the fallback.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A checker could be sensitive to perturbations yet share the same systematic blind spot if the perturbation does not probe that blind spot.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A restater will accept both the true and false variants because it echoes the claim regardless of content. A genuine verifier must reject the false variant because it checks content against an independent source. By constructing a matched pair of true and false claims and measuring the checker's discrimination, we directly test verification within a single run without needing a second engine.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
